chunks: Abu Dawud, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl, from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
The salat is an offering of every pious one.

key_terms.الصَّلَاة: Salat — the ritual prayer, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.تَقِيّ: Taqi — the God-conscious, pious, God-fearing person; one who possesses taqwa
key_terms.قُرْبَان: Qurban — an offering or sacrifice made to draw near (qaruba) to God; the word shares the same root as 'qurb' (nearness/proximity)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of salat according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), the eighth Imam, declares that the ritual prayer (salat) is the spiritual offering — the means of drawing near to God — for every God-fearing, pious person. Just as sacrifice (qurban) was the supreme act of worship and proximity to God in earlier traditions, the salat occupies this paramount position in Islam. The hadith underscores salat's role not merely as a legal obligation but as the most exalted act of devotion by which the pious soul approaches its Creator.
